title: SEC-000004: Framing, integrity and authorisation on the serial link, and demotion of the XOFF/XON control bytes
statement: The BMS master software shall accept a serial (SCI/UART, RS485) frame only after an explicit length field has been validated against the received byte count and an integrity field has been verified, shall pass only authenticated frames to the application layer, and shall treat the XOFF and XON byte values as ordinary payload unless they arrive inside a frame that has already been authenticated.
rationale: The serial receive path in the real source has no framing, no length field, no integrity field and no authorisation, and it treats two arbitrary byte values as privileged commands: any 0x13 on the line suppresses the master's transmission, and any 0x11 restores it, with no authentication and no diagnosis. A single byte placed on the line is therefore sufficient to alter the master's behaviour on that link, which is a control-injection condition even though the current consequence is limited. Framing and authentication are required together because an integrity field on an unframed stream can be forged or misaligned by the peer, and the control-byte clause is required because a value that acts as a command must not be reachable outside an authenticated frame (TARA threat THR-006, TARA mitigation MIT-005).

acceptance_criteria.measure: Bytes on the receive line that reach the application layer without passing frame-length and integrity validation, over a 24 h injection campaign
Transitions of the transmit-enabled state caused by a 0x13 or 0x11 byte outside an authenticated frame
Frames whose declared length differs from the received byte count and which are passed onward
Frames with a valid structure and a modified payload that are accepted
Diagnosis entries raised per detected receive-queue overflow

Genuine frames rejected over a 24 h campaign at nominal bus load whose observed genuine-frame population is at least 3 x 10^6 frames. Pass is 0 rejections observed over that population, which is a one-sided 95 percent upper confidence bound of 1 x 10^-6 on the rate by the rule of three (3/n <= 1e-6 for n >= 3e6). The integrity value used on this interface shall be at least 22 bits, which is the width for which a per-frame false rejection probability of 2^-w stays below the rate this criterion bounds over that population.

safety_allocation.mitigation: Security mitigation for the serial communication path. asil is recorded as not_applicable because this is a security requirement; the trace to the safety goal records that a link carrying measurement data is an interference vector for the requirements derived from that goal, not an ASIL allocation.

revision_history.author: cybersecurity_engineer
revision_history.description: Replaced the absolute '0 genuine frames rejected over 24 h' acceptance criterion with a bounded rate, a stated population the bound is demonstrated over, and a minimum integrity value width that makes the bound achievable. Remediation of finding FB2-REV-FND-000028. The old criterion was unsatisfiable and non-discriminating at the same time: a keyed integrity value of width w rejects a genuine frame with probability 2^-w, so over a 24 h campaign the expected number of genuine rejections is n * 2^-w, non-zero for any practical w; meanwhile an implementation that rejected every frame would satisfy the criterion vacuously, and would also satisfy the other criteria in this record vacuously. The new criterion is 0 rejections observed over a genuine-frame population of at least 3 x 10^6 in a 24 h campaign, which by the rule of three (0 failures in n trials gives a one-sided 95 percent upper bound of 3/n) is a bound of 1 x 10^-6 on the rate; and it requires the integrity value on the interface to be at least 22 bits, which is the width for which 2^-w stays below that rate over that population. The three statements are mutually consistent, so the criterion is now achievable by a correct implementation of adequate width and is not satisfied by an always-rejecting one (~100 percent) or by a 16-bit one (~1.5e-5 per frame). The criterion is therefore STRICTER in discriminating power than the zero it replaces, and it is also a harder engineering obligation, because it constrains the width of the integrity value where the zero constrained nothing. The absolute zeros that remain in this record are the ones that are decidable by the check existing - injected frames accepted, replayed frames accepted, length-mismatch frames reaching the callback, control-byte transitions - and those are over countable events on a channel where no collision is involved, so they are unchanged and were deliberately not relaxed. The verification measure FB2-VER-TMS-000018 and its execution record were regenerated against the new criterion in the same revision set. No ASIL value, safety_goal_ref, statement clause or verification approach was changed.

real_source_presence: Control ABSENT. src/app/driver/uart/uart.c:163 arms a single-byte interrupt-driven receive into one static byte (declared at :108). In the receive interrupt at :244-263, the values 0x13 and 0x11 (defined at src/app/driver/uart/uart.h:68-69) are consumed at :247-250 to gate transmission, and every other byte is forwarded to a queue at :254 with the enqueue return value discarded, so overflow is silent and no diagnosis entry is raised. No framing, length validation, integrity field or authorisation exists anywhere on this path. A further absence is recorded honestly and constrains the impact rating: the application consumer of this queue is a stub — FTSK_RunUserCodeUart in src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c:330-338 contains only UART_HandleFlowControl() and OS_NotifyTake() and never calls UART_Read — so no application data path from the serial receive queue to the database was found, and the evidenced impact is confined to transmit suppression and silent overflow. This requirement MUST be re-derived if the hypothetical project connects a protocol to this queue. Anchors FB2-SRC-COD-000067, FB2-SRC-COD-000068, FB2-SRC-COD-000069, FB2-SRC-COD-000070, FB2-SRC-COD-000071.
